If $X \sim \textrm{Geom}(p),$ then $X$ has the following probability mass function:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14165669/assets/8fe2487af4333bae81059a2ab221b3988bbdf27f4f51521683addd789c31a4b9.svg)

Here, $X \sim \textrm{Geom}\left(\dfrac 15\right),$ so the distribution of $X$ in this case is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14165669/assets/a44212ab1418417646876630a4cea241bfefaf063b26251dc5f157824cc4805d.svg)

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(2\le X\le 3) & =P(X\in \{2,3\}) \\  & =P(X=2)+P(X=3) \\  & =f(2)+f(3) \\  & ={(\frac{4}{5})}^{1}(\frac{1}{5})+{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{36}{125}.\end{aligned}
$$
